films.title: WHAT EVEN IS OMERTÀ? — The key needs a committee
films.concept: A Rookie holds an absurdly large key while four tiny, very serious adults hold a meeting around it. He thought he was playing a mafia game. His car becomes materials, knowledge reveals a recipe, crafting creates a key, and other people must contribute before Family approval opens a persistent archive. A clearly marked cut to another part of the same city reveals the shipment/market/investigation chain. The joke is that a basic game interaction has acquired a group project and a second genre before the Rookie has finished complaining.

thesis.recognition: Mafia hierarchy, old browser-RPG inventory, guild readiness checks, conspiracy board.
thesis.novelty: The humble key is effectively a multiplayer institution. A file archive gets a more serious launch meeting than the crime.
thesis.sensation: Key clang → crunchy salvage ticks → stamp impact → mouse-click approval → archive bass hit → notification panic. The opening is already absurd on the first frame.
thesis.patternInterrupt: A normal-sized key dominates the frame while a miniature committee points at it; Rookie: “This key needs FOUR PEOPLE?”
thesis.informationGap: Why are other people and intel necessary for a door? The viewer learns the contributions before seeing the persistent payoff.
thesis.shareTrigger: Send it to the group member who says “just one quick quest.” Three visual genres arrive before the viewer can categorize the game.

films.claimNote: F01–F09, F12–F17, F20–F23, F26–F27. Four seats are from the Foundry pilot, not every mission. “Elsewhere” at 21.0 explicitly separates the campaign example from the archive. The shipment is diverted through an authorized operation; it is not a randomly disappearing commodity. Full-release master under L01 and L05; all pictured systems are available at publication.

films.title: THE ECONOMY IS THE GAME — The chart has a Family
films.concept: The Rookie buys a bulk cargo order, survives a partial convoy ambush and pays a rival Family’s destination toll. He thinks he has understood the economy. The Auditor opens the OMR market: a canonical sale routes Hook funding into protocol liquidity, while a separate seasonal liquidity range becomes a Family siege map. The winning Family gets rights to future funded fees; the protocol keeps custody of the principal. A cardboard shipping problem has become an argument about who controls a section of the chart.

thesis.recognition: MMO trading, cargo ambushes, mafia tolls, an ETH/OMR market and guild territory wars.
thesis.novelty: A financial range map becomes a literal Family war table. Players contest funded fee rights while the pool principal stays under protocol control.
thesis.sensation: Crate slam → inventory pickup → toy convoy impact → toll bell → mechanical Hook splitter → tabletop siege → a tiny receipt instead of a stolen vault.
thesis.patternInterrupt: A cardboard cargo crate slams onto an absurd finance desk. Rookie: “I bought some cargo.”
thesis.informationGap: Why does one cargo purchase end with a Family fighting over a section of a market chart?
thesis.shareTrigger: Game friends recognize a guild turning everything into territory; crypto friends recognize the fee-rights/principal distinction. The same scene is legible to both.

films.claimNote: Full-release master under L01–L03 and L05. F10–F11, F24, F29, F32, F35–F38 and F42 apply. The Rookie owns the collected bulk cargo before dispatch; the staged ambush leaves a verified remainder. The destination is another Family’s territory, with the shipper present and funded for a positive toll. The canonical OMR sale is a separate human-confirmed action, not an automatic result of cargo trading. Hook POL funding goes to Core; designated seasonal Turf LP fees go through their own bridge. A siege settlement changes prospective rights, not historical credits or principal ownership. No tokenomics numbers, projected yield or invented receipt.

audio.voices: Rookie: baffled conversational tenor. Auditor: fast, precise midrange. Don: quiet authority, now clearly representing the rival destination Family and later that Family’s Turf victory.
audio.music: Original 126 BPM calculator-percussion breakbeat. At 13.500 add a dry mechanical bass pulse; at 18.000 an absurd two-note toy-military motif. No borrowed music or casino payoff.
audio.drops: 0.000 crate slam; 4.500 muted ambush kick; 7.500 toll bell; 15.000 Hook splitter clack; 18.000 cardboard siege impact; 24.000 small receipt click.
audio.silence: 21.000–22.500: remove music under “They get the pool?” Restart with a dry two-note answer on “The fee rights.” Remove bass again at 25.500 for “So the pool stays?”
audio.transitions: Pickup pip becomes a hi-hat; toll bell becomes the market cursor sound; splitter clack becomes a map-pin knock; siege impact resolves into a deliberately tiny receipt-printer tick.
audio.mix: No rising profit chime, cash shower or triumphant investment-return sound. Liquidity and fee events have mechanical feedback; the laugh comes from the tiny receipt after the huge siege.

films.title: THE GAME IS WATCHING YOU — The rat is a noticeboard
films.concept: The Family wants its Consigliere to identify a rat. A cheap receipt-printer adviser points at a public notice. Two people investigate different original records, but corroborating disclosure does not prove betrayal. A private participant report remains private. The players then contribute evidence and a crafted seal to an authorized operation that records a different, persistent world outcome. The printer embodies the integrated release Consigliere: it reads permitted context and prepares a proposal while the players make consequential decisions. Dialogue is scripted characterization, and the interface inserts use the released adviser. The unsettling idea is that the city can preserve what happened without pretending to know why.

thesis.recognition: Mob interrogation, “find the leaker,” conspiracy-board screenshots, AI assistant interface.
thesis.novelty: The AI-coded consigliere is office equipment with better evidence discipline than the Family. A public notice is the punchline, not a psychic betrayal detector.
thesis.sensation: Desk slam answered by printer squeak; interrogation lighting becomes fluorescent noticeboard; red string cuts into a clean permission boundary; verdict music stops on “not guilt.”
thesis.patternInterrupt: Don slams a folder onto the table. A single googly-eyed receipt printer stares back. “Find the rat.”
thesis.informationGap: Why is the suspected leak public, and why can two matching records still fail to establish guilt?
thesis.shareTrigger: People share the Family group-chat accusation and the adviser refusing to overclaim. Comment seed: what exactly does the game remember, and who is allowed to know it?

films.claimNote: F02–F09, F17, F20–F23, F26–F27, F43–F47. Full-release master under L01, L04 and L05: assume the adviser is integrated with the released campaign and command services. Its performed lines illustrate permitted reasoning rather than impersonating an actual model-call transcript. The tested campaign loop predates the opening: a route was diverted, a market established and exposed, enabling this investigation. No automatic culprit or betrayal detector exists. Not every outcome spawns a new opportunity.

audio.voices: Don leads with clipped certainty. Consigliere is calm neutral alto; no omniscient villain growl. Auditor/Detective dry and specific. Rookie supplies the human “wait” reactions.
audio.music: Original 96 BPM detuned plucked-string suspense over office ventilation. A deliberately cheap three-note mystery motif only; no recognizable mafia film score.
audio.drops: 0.000 folder slam; 1.500 printer squeak replaces expected gunshot; 10.500 two hard evidence taps; 24.000 low stamp impact on real consequence.
audio.silence: 12.000–13.500 remove music under “Disclosure. Not guilt.” Then 25.500–27.000 another music dropout for “You haven’t proved that.”
audio.transitions: Paper drag becomes surveillance room hiss; projector click becomes UI scope toggle; receipt printer resumes under end card and loops to the folder slam.
audio.mix: No jump-scare gain spike. Keep printer EQ intelligible. The silence is embarrassment, not a threat.
